Stevie Wonder is once again challenging the long-running rumor that he is not actually blind.

During a recent performance at Chicago’s United Center on Saturday, the legendary musician, 76, paused his show to mock the hearsay about his eyesight.

“If you believe I can really drive or really see, get in the car with me and we’ll see what happens to us at the end of the day,” he said from behind his piano as the audience burst into laughter.

Social media users took to X to get in on the discourse.

“Sounds exactly like what someone who wants us to believe he isn’t blind would say,” one person teased.

Another person joked, “Nahhh.. who’s relaying this information to Stevie. It’s that or he be on online reading it all too.”

Wonder has addressed the rumors in the past, telling fans during a performance in Cardiff, Wales, in July 2025 that there’s not an ounce of truth to them.

“You know there have been rumors about me seeing and all that?” the singer-songwriter said. “But seriously, you know the truth. Truth is, shortly after my birth, I became blind.”

Wonder called his disability a “blessing,” adding, “because it’s allowed me to see the world in the vision of truth, of sight. See people in the spirit of them, not how they look. Not what color they are, but what color is their spirit?”
